3.  **Integral Calculation:** For each beam $b$, compute the integral of the product of the camera ray transmittance and the photon beam transmittance over the interval $[t_c^-, t_c^+]$ [S1].

The claim states that for each beam $b$, one must compute the integral of the product of the camera ray transmittance and the photon beam transmittance over the interval $[t_c^-, t_c^+]$. Source [S1] explicitly supports this in Section 7.2.2 (implied by the notes and Equation 29). The notes state: 'Integrate the product of camera ray transmittance $e^{-σ_{t_c}}$ and photon beam transmittance $e^{-σ_{t_b}}$ over $t_c$.' Equation 29 shows the formula: $L_b(...) ≈ ... ∫_{t_c^-}^{t_c^+} e^{-σ_{t_c}} e^{-σ_{t_b}} dt_c$. The text confirms that $t_c^-$ and $t_c^+$ are the intersection distances (bounds) and the integrand is the product of the two transmittances. Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
